transcript: UT San Antonio says some people could have ankle deep water in their yard before phone warns anyone. So its researchers built a station that charges itself from light and needs no tower. Four optical sensors at different heights watch the water along with rain, temperature, humidity and light. A small chip on the station runs the AI itself, so it judges flood risk without a central server. When the risk rises, a radio signal can carry more than a half mile through city streets and up to five miles in open country to a hub. At the hub, a second larger AI model draws a map of how flooding could spread for emergency responders. The university reports 98.82 percent validation accuracy from early assessments after training and no field result. It names no town that has installed one. Deployment is still the goal.
